articles.title: The bug that only existed on the platform nobody was looking at
articles.excerpt: I ship a Python tool with a regression suite of several thousand checks and CI on ubuntu, macOS and None of them errored. Each was a rule that was true on the machine it was written on. The tool has a…
articles.body: I ship a Python tool with a regression suite of several thousand checks and CI on ubuntu, macOS and Windows at Python 3.8 and 3.13. Yesterday all five jobs were green. Today those same jobs turned up four defects that had already shipped. None of them errored. Each was a rule that was true on the machine it was written on. 1. A guard that compared a resolved path to an unresolved one The tool has a command that reads one file into the model's context. It refuses a symlink that a repository chose whose target sits outside that repository — a repo shipping docs/notes.md -> ~/.ssh/id_rsa should not get that file read aloud. The guard looked like this: root = find_root () # returns a RESOLVED path named_inside = any ( r in Path ( os . path . abspath ( target )).

articles.title: SteelSeries Aeon Pro Review So Far
articles.excerpt: The SteelSeries Aeon Pro packs in just about every "pro" feature you could ask for in a controller, with Hall-effect thumbsticks, tactile switch buttons, adjustable triggers, and the company's outstan…
articles.body: The SteelSeries Aeon Pro is one of the most advanced controllers I've ever tested. It's also the most expensive – but it brings some features never before seen in a controller. Notably, the Aeon Pro borrows the outstanding "infinite battery" system from the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro line of gaming headsets . Instead of relying on a cable or dock to charge the controller, the Aeon Pro has two rechargeable batteries – one in the controller and another that charges in the base station. Like the Nova Pro, when one battery runs out of juice, you simply pop it out and swap it with the fully-charged one from the base station. In less than 10 seconds, your controller is fully juiced up and the previously depleted battery is tucked back in the dock to charge.

articles.title: Why this month's Microsoft patch release is a doozy
articles.excerpt: Security gnomes are pumping out patches ahead of an expected onslaught of AI-assisted attacks.
articles.body: Microsoft’s patch for September is a doozy, with a record number of roughly 972 vulnerabilities fixed and 112 of them meeting the high critical-severity threshold. It was only two months ago that Microsoft patched a then-record 570 vulnerabilities. Then, last month, Microsoft patched some 620 of them. Google and other companies have also published record numbers of vulnerabilities in recent months. Two weeks ago, OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon Web Services, Google, Microsoft, and 100 companies and organizations published an open letter warning of a narrowing window for patching vulnerabilities ahead of an expected tsunami of AI-enabled attacks that actively exploit them first. The industry is taking the threat seriously by pumping out unprecedented numbers of patches in their software.

articles.title: Did Venus eat its own moon?
articles.excerpt: Scientists may finally know why Venus, Earth's twin, lacks a moon, finding that the hottest planet in the solar system may have consumed its own natural satellite.
articles.body: Scientists may finally know why Venus, Earth's twin, lacks a moon, finding that the hottest planet in the solar system may have consumed its own natural satellite. Venus is often referred to as Earth's twin due to its size, mass, rocky composition, and distance from the sun, but there are some glaring differences between the two planets. Aside from Venus' blisteringly hot temperature, which could melt lead, incredible surface pressure, violent high-speed winds, and clouds of sulfuric acid, one of the key differences between Earth and Venus can be seen from afar. While our planet has a constant companion in the form of the moon , Venus lacks a moon of its own.
